name: The Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB)
description: The Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB) is a family of verification, search, counting, frequency-estimation, and collision tasks over the digits of Pi. It is designed as an architecture-neutral specification of mathematically fixed instances, classical comparators, resource boundaries, and admissible claims. The specification fixes zero-based indexing, binary and hexadecimal digit conventions, dense and sparse candidate domains, and task-specific payloads for target-bearing and collision problems. It separates three independent properties that benchmark descriptions can conflate: digit access (lookup or direct), oracle-construction provenance (P0–P4), and controller blindness (B0 or B1). A non-total capability grid retains codes R0–R12 as stable claim labels while stating their named dependencies; a higher-numbered code does not automatically inherit every lower-numbered capability. The evidence protocol requires pre-execution validation, routed-resource accounting, preservation of raw outcomes, outcome-independent eligibility, visible conditioning, uncertainty estimates, protocol separation, and formal record freezing. Collision scaling is stated as a heuristic candidate-domain model: birthday behavior gives D_h = Θ(16^(h/2)), while element distinctness gives O(D_h^(2/3)) coherent queries only under declared access and memory assumptions. These query bounds do not establish the earliest repeat, a quantum frontier, or end-to-end advantage.
